# Product Marketing Context

**Document version:** v1
**Last updated:** 2026-10-20

## Product Overview
**One-liner:** A free, anonymous love-language assessment for Indonesian couples — 25 statements, a ranked profile, and AI-generated advice in Bahasa Indonesia.
**What it does:** Walks a participant through 25 Likert-scale statements across Gary Chapman's five love languages, ranks their results, and delivers a personalised two-paragraph advice text generated by AI. Results live at a permanent shareable URL — no account needed, no data retained beyond what the participant chooses to save.
**Product category:** Relationship self-assessment tool / personality quiz
**Product type:** Free web app (no accounts, no paywall)
**Business model:** Free public tool; no monetisation currently present.

## Target Audience
**Target companies:** N/A — direct consumer (B2C)
**Decision-makers:** Individual adults in relationships (any gender, any stage of relationship)
**Primary use case:** Self-discovery — understanding how you express and receive affection so you and your partner can connect more intentionally.
**Jobs to be done:**
- "Help me understand my love language so I can communicate better with my partner."
- "Give me something shareable I can send my partner so we can talk about this."
- "Give me honest, personalised advice, not a generic quiz result."
**Use cases:**
- Solo reflection on relational patterns
- Sharing results with a partner to spark a conversation
- Returning to a saved result link to re-read advice

## Personas
| Persona | Cares about | Challenge | Value we promise |
|---------|-------------|-----------|------------------|
| Individual (solo taker) | Self-awareness, relational growth | Doesn't know why certain things feel more loving than others | A clear, ranked profile + warm AI advice in their language |
| Couple (partner shares result) | Mutual understanding | Can't articulate what they need from each other | A shareable link that opens the conversation without confrontation |

## Problems & Pain Points
**Core problem:** People in relationships often feel unseen or misunderstood, but can't articulate why — they lack a shared vocabulary for how affection is expressed and received.
**Why alternatives fall short:**
- Generic online quizzes give a label with no depth or actionable advice
- English-language tools (Gary Chapman's official site, etc.) aren't localised for Indonesian cultural context or language
- Couples therapy is expensive and carries stigma for early-stage relationship questions
**What it costs them:** Ongoing friction, misread intentions, feeling unloved even when love is being expressed — just in a different language.
**Emotional tension:** "Am I asking for too much? Does my partner even care? Why does nothing feel like enough?"

## Competitive Landscape
**Direct:** Gary Chapman's official quiz (5lovelanguages.com) — English only, no personalised advice, no shareable result link.
**Secondary:** BuzzFeed / generic personality quizzes — superficial, no scoring depth, no advice, not relationship-focused.
**Indirect:** Couples therapy, relationship self-help books — high cost or high effort; no quick, digital entry point.

*(No competitor mentions found in the codebase — these are inferred from the product category.)*

## Differentiation
**Key differentiators:**
- Fully in Bahasa Indonesia — UI, advice, brand voice
- AI-generated personalised advice (not canned text), generated once and stored with the result
- Permanent shareable result URL with no login required
- Privacy-forward: no email, no tracking, opaque token access only
- Calm, premium, anti-cliché visual identity — no hearts, no wedding imagery
**How we do it differently:** The assessment generates a unique piece of advice per person via an AI agent, rather than mapping scores to pre-written buckets.
**Why that's better:** Participants feel seen, not categorised. The advice reads like it was written for them.
**Why customers choose us:** Indonesian language, no friction (no signup), shareable result, warm and intentional brand that doesn't feel like a dating app.

## Objections
| Objection | Response |
|-----------|----------|
| "Is this based on real psychology?" | Built on Gary Chapman's canonical five love languages framework, used in relationship counselling worldwide. |
| "What happens to my data?" | No account, no email, no tracking. Your result is only accessible via the private link you save. |
| "What if I disagree with my result?" | The advice is personalised — but you know yourself best. Use it as a starting point for reflection, not a verdict. |

**Anti-persona:** Anyone looking for couples therapy, a dating app, matchmaking, or wedding planning tools — the brand explicitly is not those things.

## Switching Dynamics
**Push:** Frustration with English-only tools that don't reflect Indonesian relational norms or language; distrust of quizzes that feel shallow or gamified.
**Pull:** Free, fast (25 questions), private, produces something worth sharing — lowers the bar to start the conversation with a partner.
**Habit:** "We just talk about it ourselves" — the informal approach of not naming the dynamic.
**Anxiety:** "What if my result says something uncomfortable?" / "What if my partner and I are mismatched?"

- "Kayaknya kita nggak nyambung aja." *(It feels like we just don't click.)*
**How they describe us:**
- *(No testimonials yet — product appears pre-launch or early-stage)*
**Words to use:** Hubungan (relationship), kasih sayang (affection/love), tumbuh bersama (grow together), memahami (understand), penilaian (assessment), profil (profile), saran (advice)
**Words to avoid:** Dating, jodoh (soulmate/matchmaking), pernikahan (wedding/marriage) as a primary frame, terapi (therapy)

## Brand Voice
| Attribute | Means | Doesn't mean | Example line |
|-----------|-------|--------------|--------------|
| Calm | Measured, unhurried, confident | Cold, flat, clinical | "Temukan bagaimana Anda mengekspresikan dan menerima kasih sayang." |
| Warm | Caring, human, personal | Gushing, over-the-top romantic | AI advice is two paragraphs, conversational, direct to "kamu" |
| Premium | Intentional, high-craft, no clutter | Expensive, exclusive, gatekept | No hearts or wedding imagery; restrained palette |
| Intentional | Every element has a reason | Rigid, over-designed | Logo = two weighted dots + curve; the period in the brand name |

**Tone by context:**
- Support: Gentle, clear, no jargon — guide without condescending
- Launch: Quiet confidence — "this exists, it's good, try it"
- Errors: Calm, non-blaming — never technical error text shown to users
- Sales: N/A (no sales flow currently)
- Social: Warm and thoughtful, not viral-bait

**Terms we own:** `relationship project.` (the period is the mark)
**Never use (and why):** Hearts/cupid/ring emoji — conflicts with "not a dating app" positioning; pure white backgrounds — off-brand (warm cream palette only); "platform" — this is a focused single-purpose tool, not a platform.
